answer: Stake-bonding is the core Sybil defence: each agent identity must lock a minimum bond in a custody vault, and the registry reads that balance, not signatures, so cloned keys cannot split one deposit. A small proof-of-work inlet burns compute per registration, and per-bond rate limits stop one funded wallet from fanning out cheap clones. Flooding with fake agents thus costs a full bond plus energy each, and colluding nodes forfeit stake, pushing marginal cost above expected reward; payouts wait out a challenge window, making a zephyr of fresh accounts slow and expensive.
